mechanism.summary: beam_cross_prev (sigma_b) is a one-step-lagged physics INPUT to the cathode/beam solve. It enters at cablp/cathode/circuit_idriven.py:1180 as PlasmaState(sigma_b=beam_cross_prev[cathode_index]) and sets l_b / beam_bypass_fraction / long_mfp at :886-888, the bypass fraction and the anode ledger.

order.sigma_b_consumed: the previous step's SSPRK stage-2 write -- a STAGE-state value. THE LAG.

measured_map_before.accept_boundary: solver.py:5504 _restore_step_cache(attempt.solver_cache) sets the cache to #5's write -- the stage-state value #1 then consumes.
measured_map_before.why_no_pure_reorder_exists: #1 is the only solve at the accepted state that writes sigma_b; #2 and #3 are converged precisely BECAUSE #1 wrote first. Moving the trigger after suggest_timestep does not help (#2 is update_cache=False and touches nothing). Moving it before the cache restore hands it the step-START cache -- more lagged, wrong state. The epilogue's other accepted-state solves (idriven_result_evaluator solver.py:5640, idriven_vdis_evaluator solver.py:5805) cannot refresh sigma_b at all: they build PlasmaState(sigma_b=beam_cross_prev[idx]) and return a SolverResult with no beam march and no beam_atten_cross (physics/cathode.py:790-890).

mechanism.lag_map_convergence: One iteration. The pair (#2, #3) consumes #1's write and reproduces it; measured 1199/1199 'pair consumes exactly the trigger's sigma_b write' and 1199/1199 '#2 == #3'.

edits.change: Gained an optional cathode_solve argument naming WHICH solve to read. None keeps every historical caller's reading (the cached solve of record). The phase trigger passes its converged accepted-state solve.

A single-entry memo over READ-ONLY (update_cache=False) solves. A cache-writing solve never consults or populates it: its job is the write, not the value. On a hit the memoized result is returned without re-solving; on any miss the solve runs fresh and replaces the entry. A stale memo is never served.
The memo key. Compared with == over raw-byte encodings rather than hashed, so there is no collision channel and -0.0/0.0 and last-ulp differences separate.

memo_key.principle: THE INTERFACE LESSON: sigma_b is an INPUT to this solve, so keying on (state, time) alone would have served one lag state for another -- exactly the defect being removed.
components: state (AFTER _smoothed_sample_state, so the sample EMA is covered)
memo_key.excluded_and_why: floors, ion_mass_g, mu, geometry, input_dict, I_ion, gas_type -- assigned once in __init__ and never mutated anywhere in solver.py (verified by grep for in-place assignment/update/pop), so they cannot separate two calls within one run.
memo_key.invalidation: None needed and none added. Correctness is carried entirely by key completeness, which is why a rejected attempt, a Picard restore and _restore_step_cache all remain safe: they move key components, so the next lookup misses.

disclosed_residuals.status: OUT OF SCOPE, LEFT IN PLACE by ruling
disclosed_residuals.detail: The accepted-step epilogue's power-balance warming re-solve (solver.py:5640 idriven_result_evaluator) and current-driven circuit advance (solver.py:5805 idriven_vdis_evaluator) BOTH consume the stage-state sigma_b at the accepted state -- the same lag, at a second site the 1c diagnostic did not describe. They were found by this member's mapping pass and deliberately not touched. They cannot be fixed by ordering alone: running the trigger earlier in the epilogue would refresh sigma_b for them but would also hand the trigger the pre-advance _circuit_I_loop, changing the trigger's INPUTS.

main_discharge-phase trajectories are expected to move at the diagnostic's measured class -- median ~5e-12, tails to 4e-1 on beam-family internals where long_mfp flips. This is invisible to gate 2's horizon and that is not a gate weakness but a property of the regime: sigma_b at the launch cell is 0 or ~4.2e-14 through pre-breakdown, and both land in the same long_mfp branch, so the lagged and converged inputs produce bit-identical SolverResults there. Measured: the trigger's solve already equalled the pair's on 1199/1199 pre-change steps. THE R3-TIP TIER C PAIR IS THE INSTRUMENT that will see the discharge-phase movement.
disclosed_residuals.consequence: The 4k A/B's BIT-IDENTICAL verdict certifies that the dedupe and the memo introduced NO arithmetic change; it does NOT certify that the member is a no-op over a full cycle, and must not be quoted as if it did.

disclosed_residuals.detail: self._cathode_solve (and _cathode_x0 / _cathode_x0_twin) still come from the refresher, i.e. the lagged solve, so every existing diagnostic, census and warm-start continuation reads exactly what it read before and nothing else moved. Only the trigger's threshold input was redirected. Re-pointing the solve of record at the converged solve is a separate question and was not taken.
